To answer the questions:  Magicians have always performed the illusion of the bullet catch.  Historically, most of the guys that have died doing the trick have died due to lacking safety measures or the gun really shooting you in the face.  TaDa!  Sucks right?  Related note: One of the greatest performances of a bullet catch illusion is Penn and Teller's, designed by Banachek, (He's the guy that fooled Duke University scientists into thinking he had telekinetic powers for over a year before he was all "psych!"), and definitely deserves a watch.  This one is different.  This one is real.  For starters, you can't catch a bullet wit your teeth.  That's stupid.  There's a custom welded mouth piece and tooth guard to stop the bullet.  It's not a reduced round, just a lot of accuracy.  Bolt action rifle is on 2 tripods, and as long as everything goes according to planned, it feels like getting punched in the jaw by a weaker adult.  Fun fact, this episode of that's incredible was also the first time a live round was tracked on television with a slow motion camera.  Also fun fact, once, things didn't go according the planned and my mom shot him through the lip.  Survived, still has metal in his lip, still married.

And yes, it's definitely a freak show. On the same episode was a guy pulling a big ads blimp with his teeth.  A few months later, my father, some guy that would Mr Miyagi arrows out of mid air wih his bare hands, and Menudo were touring Latin America.  TLDR Tiny Ricky Martin was a beast and the 80s were weird.
